answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Valid agents blossom in a curated orchard of trust, where each identity bond acts as a cryptographic mirror of verifiable hardware state. Attackers cannot forge credentials without staking collateral that scales superlinearly: registering a Sybil swarm incurs exponential capital exhaustion, making mass spoofing economically unviable.
